chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

If you have a need from Allāh, the Glorified, then begin by seeking Allāh’s blessing on His Messenger, may Allāh bless him and his descendants, then ask your need, because Allāh is too generous to accept one (seeking His blessing on His Messenger) of the two requests made to Him and deny the other.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for making dua to ensure both the request and the blessing on the Prophet are accepted?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) advises that when supplicating to God for a specific need, one should first send blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). This practice ensures that both requests—the blessing on the Prophet and the personal need—are granted, as God is too generous to accept one and reject the other. In Shia tradition, this highlights the concept of *tawassul* (seeking intercession) through the Prophet, viewing the act of sending blessings as a means of elevating the status of the supplicant before making their request.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 361. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

If you have a need from Allāh, the Glorified, then begin by seeking Allāh’s blessing on His Messenger, may Allāh bless him and his descendants, then ask your need, because Allāh is too generous to accept one (seeking His blessing on His Messenger) of the two requests made to Him and deny the other.
